goal: The database client has one statement counter that is off unless a test or a log line asks, an integration test holds the statements of five admin screens in a baseline that only falls, and each admin render logs one line with its count.
why: Nothing counts queries today, so the store Home grew to 30 statements unseen. After this step the store shell, the store Home, the orders list, the products list and the platform Home each have a number in src/server/admin-statements.baseline.json, and a change that adds one statement fails pnpm test:int.

commits.title: A statement counter in the database client, off unless asked

changes.how: A module with no import but node:async_hooks (it must not import 'server-only', drizzle or pg, so tests and scripts can load it). Export type StatementRecord = { text: string; values: unknown[]; rows: number | null; ms: number; control: boolean } where control is true for a statement whose trimmed lower-case text starts with 'begin', 'commit', 'rollback', 'savepoint', 'release' or 'set local'. Keep one AsyncLocalStorage<{ statements: StatementRecord[] }>. Export countStatements<T>(run: () => Promise<T>): Promise<{ result: T; statements: StatementRecord[]; count: number; ms: number }>: it runs 'run' inside a fresh store and returns what was recorded; count is the number of records whose control is false. Export noteStatement(text, values): it returns null when no store is running and no render counter is set (the common case: do nothing, allocate nothing); otherwise it pushes a record (rows null, ms 0) and returns a function done(rows) that fills rows and ms. Export statementsOf(key: object): a WeakMap-backed counter for renders: renderCounter() returns the object React's cache() hands out for the current render (see the next commit) and noteStatement also adds 1 to it when one is active. To keep this file free of React, export setRenderCounter(get: (() => { statements: number } | null) | null): the admin layout's module sets it once. Export sameStatementTwice(records): the list of texts that appear twice or more with JSON-equal values, for later budgets. The functions never throw: wrap their bodies so that a failure inside the counter cannot fail a query.

In create(), after 'pool.on("error", () => {});', add: pool.on('connect', (client) => { ... }) that replaces client.query with a wrapper once per client. The wrapper reads the statement's text (the first argument when it is a string, else its .text) and values (the first argument's .values, else the second argument when it is an array), calls noteStatement(text, values) from './statement-count', and then calls the original query with the same arguments and the same 'this'. When noteStatement returned null, return the original's result untouched. When it returned done, and the original returned a promise, return that same promise after attaching result.then((r) => done(r?.rowCount ?? r?.rows?.length ?? null), () => done(null)) to a separate branch (do not replace the promise the caller awaits, and add no await). When the caller passed a callback (the last argument is a function), call done(null) and return the original's result. Both pools get it, because create() makes the primary and the replica. Change nothing else in this file: withRows(), db(), replicaDb(), readDb(), longerTimeout() and closeDb() stay as they are.

An integration test (it runs with pnpm test:int against DATABASE_URL). Cases: (1) outside countStatements nothing is recorded: run db().execute(sql`select 1`) and assert noteStatement('x', []) returns null. (2) inside countStatements, two db().execute calls give count 2, and each record has the statement's text, its values (select ${7}::int gives values [7]) and rows 1. (3) a db().transaction with one insert into a temp table and one select gives count 2 and two control records (begin, commit). (4) two countStatements running at once (Promise.all) do not see each other's statements. (5) the same select sent twice with the same value is reported by sameStatementTwice(). (6) a statement that fails (select 1/0) is recorded with rows null and the error still reaches the caller.

It compares each figure to src/server/admin-statements.baseline.json: a figure above the baseline fails with 'this screen now sends N statements, baseline M: read less, or raise the baseline in this commit and say why in the commit message'; a figure below fails with 'run UPDATE_BASELINE=1 pnpm test:int src/server/admin-statements.int.test.ts'. With the environment variable UPDATE_BASELINE=1 the test writes the file with what it measured and passes. A last case checks the counter's record for the store shell lists each statement's text, values and rows. A 'would notice' case wraps storeShellReads with one extra db().execute(sql`select 1`) and asserts the count is the baseline plus 1.

commits.title: Each admin render logs one line with its statements

changes.how: Server-only. 'export const renderCount = cache(() => ({ statements: 0, started: Date.now() }))' with cache from 'react'. On module load call setRenderCounter(() => { try { return renderCount(); } catch { return null; } }) from '@/db/statement-count'. Outside a render React's cache() returns a fresh object on each call, so a job or a route handler adds to an object nobody reads: that is intended.

In Gate, after the account is known, take 'const counted = renderCount()' and register 'after(() => log("info", "admin.render", { statements: counted.statements, ms: Date.now() - counted.started }))' with after from 'next/server' and log from '@/server/log'. The line holds two numbers and nothing else: no path, no account, no store, no statement text (D400).

A unit test that reads src/app/admin/(gated)/layout.tsx as text and asserts the admin.render line passes only the fields statements and ms, and that src/db/statement-count.ts contains no call of log( or console.

Add a section '## Statements per screen' after '## The admin as people use it': the five figures from the baseline, the rule (a change that adds a read to the shell or a home screen raises a number in src/server/admin-statements.baseline.json in the same commit and says why), how to count anything (countStatements() from src/db/statement-count.ts) and that production's figure is the admin.render log line.

Do not wrap pool.query as well as client.query: pool.query calls client.query inside, so a statement would count twice.
Do not call requireMemberAny(), requirePermission() or requirePlatformReader() from the int test, and do not add a bypass to sign-in for it.

checked_in_code: I opened src/db/client.ts: create() builds a pg Pool and drizzle on it, for the primary and the replica, and transactions run on a pooled client, so the counter is hung on each client at the pool's 'connect' event rather than on pool.query as finding AD-12 says (that would miss every statement inside a transaction). I read the five screens' files: the store shell's reads are storesOf, waitingCount, starterOfStore and pausedAfter in [store]/layout.tsx; AD-12's storeShellData() does not exist, so the brief creates src/server/admin-screens.ts and makes the screens call it.
